audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL and CL interfaces: hardfork activation (EIP-2070), Prague state management, blob fee economics (EIP-7918), precompile gas repricing (EIP-1108), cryptographic hash functions, transaction validation exceptions (Prague), wire protocol versioning (EIP-4938), EVM block instructions (Cancun), warm COINBASE (EIP-3651), and beacon chain withdrawals (EIP-4895). The CL is in scope due to EIP-4895 withdrawal processing and EIP-7918 blob fee interactions.

in_scope: State Transition (account ops, storage, transient storage)
EVM Opcode Execution (block instructions, gas accounting)

misclassified_entities.reason: Hash Function Caller is an internal EL component (transaction validation, state root computation), not an external entity. It resides within the system boundary.
Hash512 Function Caller is an internal component (used in Ethash), not external to the system.
Contract Logic in EIP-141 refers to smart contract code executing within the EVM, which is internal to the EL.
Validated Transaction in EIP-2681 is an internal construct — a transaction that has already passed validation within the EL.
EVM Execution Context in EIP-2681 is an internal EL component executing smart contract code.
Withdrawal Processing System in EIP-4895 is an internal EL component that iterates through withdrawals in the payload.
EIP Authors in EIP-2070 represent a governance/specification process, not a runtime data source that sends data into the system.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. All transaction content (signatures, nonces, fees, blob data, authorization lists) is potentially malicious and must be fully validated. Covers EXT-TX-SUBMITTER across EIP-3651, Prague Exceptions, EIP-2681, EIP-7685, EIP-2, and EXT-TRANSACTION from EIP-141.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes broadcast blocks, transactions, and state data over unauthenticated P2P network. Peers may send invalid blocks, deprecated message types (GetNodeData on eth/67), or malicious data. Covers EXT-PEER-NODE from EIP-2070, EIP-4938, EXT-PEER from EIP-7918, and EXT-SNAP-PEER from EIP-4938.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL communicates via JWT-authenticated Engine API. Channel is authenticated but payload content (withdrawals, PREVRANDAO, block parameters) must be validated. Covers EXT-CONSENSUS-LAYER and EXT-CONSENSUS-VALIDATOR from EIP-4895, and EXT-BEACON-CHAIN from Cancun block instructions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer / Validator
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block header fields (coinbase, timestamp, PREVRANDAO, withdrawals_root, excess_blob_gas)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers set environmental data in block headers. Proposers can manipulate timestamps within bounds, choose coinbase address, and control blob inclusion. Covers EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER from Cancun block instructions, EIP-4895, EIP-7918, and EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER from EIP-7918.

trusted_external_entities.name: Smart Contract via Precompile Call
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any smart contract can invoke precompiles with arbitrary input data. Input must be validated for length, format, and curve membership. Covers EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER from EIP-1108, EXT-UNTRUSTED-INPUT from EIP-1108, and EXT-CALLING-CONTRACT from BLAKE2F.

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted Data Source via Network/RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Any data ingestion point (P2P messages, RPC calls, block data)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Generic untrusted data requiring cryptographic verification via hash functions. Covers EXT-UNTRUSTED-SOURCE from crypto hash security boundary subgraph.

trusted_external_entities.name: Ethereum Network (Fork Coordination)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block number / timestamp reaching fork activation threshold
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network state determines fork activation. Malicious peers could attempt to mislead nodes about network state. Covers EXT-NETWORK from EIP-2070.

trusted_external_entities.name: Local Builder Configuration
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Local configuration is under operator control and authenticated by filesystem permissions. Content must still be validated (non-negative, within protocol bounds). Covers EXT-BUILDER-CONFIG from EIP-7872.

trusted_external_entities.name: Fork Protocol Parameters
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Protocol parameters are compiled into the client and authenticated via the software release process. Covers EXT-FORK-PARAMS from EIP-7872.

trusted_external_entities.name: Physical Network Environment
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network conditions are outside system control and can be manipulated (eclipse attacks, bandwidth throttling). Covers EXT-NETWORK-ENVIRONMENT from EIP-7872.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Transactions in Mempool
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Blob transactions in the mempool originate from untrusted users via P2P gossip or RPC. Covers EXT-BLOB-TXS from EIP-7872.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: signature s-value check (EIP-2), nonce limit check (EIP-2681), fee structure validation (maxFeePerGas >= baseFee, priority fee <= maxFee), transaction type validation, authorization list validation (EIP-7702), blob data validation (versioned hashes, blob gas limits, blob fee sufficiency), and init code size limits.

All block data from peers must be fully validated. Deprecated message types (GetNodeData/NodeData in eth/67) must be rejected. Block headers must be validated for correct fork rules, excess_blob_gas must match recalculation, and withdrawals_root must match computed trie root.

JWT authentication verifies the channel. Withdrawal data content must be validated: withdrawal indices must be monotonically increasing, amounts must be valid Gwei values convertible to Wei without overflow, and withdrawals_root must match the Merkle-Patricia trie root computed from the withdrawal list.

PREVRANDAO value from beacon chain is authenticated via Engine API JWT. However, validators can predict the value one slot ahead. Contracts must not rely on PREVRANDAO for high-value randomness without additional entropy.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block Header Validation (coinbase, timestamp, excess_blob_gas, withdrawals_root)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block proposer controls coinbase address and timestamp within protocol bounds. Validators must verify: timestamp is within acceptable range, excess_blob_gas matches calculation (including reserve price logic from EIP-7918), and withdrawals_root matches computed value. COINBASE is pre-warmed (EIP-3651) so gas accounting must be consistent.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Precompile Execution (0x06 ECADD, 0x07 ECMUL, 0x08 Pairing, 0x09 BLAKE2F)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All precompile inputs are untrusted. ECADD/ECMUL/Pairing require: input length validation, point-on-curve verification. BLAKE2F requires: exactly 213 bytes input, final flag in {0,1}. Gas costs must be deducted before execution (150 for ECADD, 6000 for ECMUL, 34000k+45000 for Pairing, rounds*1 for BLAKE2F).

Hash functions accept arbitrary byte input. Security relies on collision resistance of Keccak. All data integrity checks depend on deterministic, collision-resistant hashing across all client implementations.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Fork Activation Logic (block number / timestamp check)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Fork activation must be deterministic based on block number or timestamp. Nodes must apply correct consensus rules based on fork status. Misidentification of fork state leads to consensus failures.

Configuration value must be validated: non-negative integer, clamped to min(protocol_max, user_value), with floor of 1 if result is zero. Filesystem permissions protect against unauthorized modification.
Protocol parameters are trusted as compiled into client binary. Incorrect parameters would cause consensus failures. Software release process and reproducible builds provide integrity.
Network conditions are adversarial. Builders must configure blob limits appropriate to bandwidth. Eclipse attacks and bandwidth throttling are possible. Block propagation timing is not guaranteed.

Blob transactions from mempool are untrusted. Full validation of blob versioned hashes, gas limits, and fee sufficiency is required before block inclusion. Builder must respect configured blob limits.
